content: 1. Swelling of the lymph nodes may occur. 2. Swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat can happen. 3. Difficulty swallowing or a sensation of throat tightness may develop. 4. Itching, skin rashes, or pale red bumps on the skin, known as hives, may appear. 5. Nausea or vomiting can occur. 6. Dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting may be experienced. 7. Stomach cramps may develop. 8. Joint pain can occur. Precautions: Who should not use rabeprazole? 9. Individuals allergic to rabeprazole, Aciphex, other proton pump inhibitors, or any ingredients in the specific product should not use rabeprazole. 10. Your pharmacist can provide a complete list of ingredients in the rabeprazole products they stock. Drug Interactions: 11. Rabeprazole should not be taken with certain other medications. 12. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription, over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using. 13. Refer to the Interactions section for more details. Important Information Before Using Rabeprazole: 14. Do not take rabeprazole unless prescribed by a healthcare provider. 15. Take rabeprazole exactly as prescribed. 16. Do not share rabeprazole with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. 17. Keep rabeprazole out of reach of children. 18. Do not chew, cut, or crush rabeprazole tablets. 19. Antacids may be taken with rabeprazole if needed. 20. Rabeprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn; it may take 1 to 4 days to fully work. What to Tell Your Healthcare Provider Before Using Rabeprazole: 21. Inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions and any medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are using. 22. This information helps determine if rabeprazole is appropriate for you. Current and Past Health Conditions: 23. Inform your healthcare provider if you have low blood potassium (hypokalemia), low blood magnesium (hypomagnesemia), low blood calcium (hypocalcemia), or liver problems. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: 24. It is unknown if rabeprazole affects pregnancy or harms an unborn baby. 25. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. 26. Your healthcare provider will advise if rabeprazole is safe during pregnancy. 27. It is unknown if rabeprazole passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions with Foods or Drinks: 28. Rabeprazole can typically be taken with or without food. 29. For duodenal ulcers or H. pylori infections, take rabeprazole after a meal. 30. It is unknown if alcohol consumption affects rabeprazole. Drug Interactions with Other Medications: 31. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using. 32. Discuss specific medications such as methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, tacrolimus, and certain antiretroviral medicines (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir) before using rabeprazole. 33. Rabeprazole may affect the absorption of some medications. Overdose: 34. If you or someone else has taken too much rabeprazole, seek medical help immediately, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose: 35. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. 36. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. 37. Do not take double or extra doses. Side Effects: 38. Common side effects include pain, sore throat, gas, infection, constipation, headache (in children aged 12 to 17), diarrhea (in children aged 12 to 17), nausea and vomiting (in children aged 12 to 17), and stomach pain (in children aged 12 to 17). 39. Contact your healthcare provider if you experience bothersome side effects. Serious Side Effects: 40. Kidney problems, such as acute tubulointerstitial nephritis, may occur. Seek medical attention if you notice decreased urine output or blood in your urine. 41. Antibiotic-associated diarrhea caused by Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) overgrowth may occur. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in stool, severe stomach cramps, or fever. Contact your healthcare provider immediately. 42. Severe skin reactions, such as Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN), may occur. Symptoms include painful red or purple skin that peels, flat red rashes, blisters, or red, watery eyes. Stop rabeprazole and seek emergency help immediately. 43. Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS) may occur, affecting multiple organs. Symptoms include rash, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the legs, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Stop rabeprazole and seek immediate medical attention. 44. Lupus or worsening of lupus symptoms may occur. Inform your provider if you experience new or worsening joint pain or a rash on your arms or cheeks. 45. Long-term use of rabeprazole may lead to vitamin B-12 deficiency. Symptoms include a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling/numbness in the hands or feet. 46. Rabeprazole may cause low magnesium levels (hypomagnesemia), which can lead to seizures or heart rhythm problems. Symptoms include changes in heart rate, dizziness, muscle spasms, or seizures. 47. Bone loss and fractures may occur, especially in older adults or those taking high doses or using rabeprazole long-term. 48. Serious allergic reactions may occur. Symptoms include breathing problems, wheezing, racing heart, fever, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, difficulty swallowing, itching, rash, hives, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, or stomach cramps. Stop rabeprazole and seek immediate medical help.
